sections.h2: Which offices bill a Buffalo house
sections.html:
Two governments bill a Buffalo house. The City of Buffalo Department of Assessment and Taxation values the property and sends the city tax and sewer rent bills. Erie County Real Property Tax Services handles the county bill. Buffalo's 2025 population estimate is 274,613.

OfficeWhat it handlesWhere and how to reach it
City Assessment and TaxationAssessments, exemptions, city tax, sewer rent, local charges such as sidewalk or demolition billsCity Hall, Room 101, 65 Niagara Square; 716-851-5733 (option 1 reaches the Assessor); 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
Erie County Real Property Tax ServicesThe county bill, online lookup and payment95 Franklin Street, Room 100; tax line 716-858-8333
Buffalo Board of Assessment ReviewHears assessment complaints filed during the December windowCity Hall, same address as Assessment and Taxation

sections.h2: Due dates for the city and county bills
sections.html:
The city bill and the county bill come from different offices on different schedules. Ask the City of Buffalo Department of Assessment and Taxation for the current due dates on the city bill, and Erie County Real Property Tax Services for the county bill.

The city's Tax Office also prepares the delinquent tax notices required under section 593 of the City Charter. If you fall behind, the department helps owners obtain court-ordered payment plans, and it notifies owners facing foreclosure for non-payment. Call 716-851-5733 early rather than after a notice arrives.

sections.h2: Annual reassessment and how to appeal
sections.html:
Buffalo has returned to annual reassessments, and owners appeal during an annual grievance window. Ask the Department of Assessment and Taxation for this year's dates, and prepare your evidence before the window opens.

You file state form RP-524 with the department, and a board of city residents with real estate experience reviews it. The city's budget describes plans for electronic filing and self-scheduled hearings. The Assessor reviews every sale and every deed filed in the city, and inspects old and new buildings, demolitions and fire-damaged structures, which is why a recent sale next door can move your number.

The department also works with the Corporation Counsel on court cases that challenge a value and on small claims assessment review applications, so an owner who loses before the board still has a next step. Bring your own evidence to the first review: a closing statement, an appraisal, or photos of damage a field inspector could have missed.

The department processes applications and renewals for several programs under the state's property tax law:

  • School Tax Relief (STAR)
  • Senior citizen exemption for low-income owners
  • Exemption for persons with disabilities and limited income
  • Senior citizen longtime resident exemption
  • Alternative exemption for military service
  • Capital improvements exemption

The state Tax Department now pays STAR as a credit after you register once, and it issues the payment before school tax is due. If you sell, close that registration. A buyer registers once the house becomes their primary residence. Eligibility rules differ by program, so the Assessor's office is the place to confirm which ones your house qualifies for.

sections.h2: What a Buffalo tax foreclosure looks like
sections.html:
The city runs an In Rem foreclosure each year and ends it with an annual auction administered by the Tax Office. Owners who fall behind get notice first, and the department can help arrange a court-ordered payment plan. Erie County also conducts auctions and foreclosure proceedings for unpaid county tax through its Real Property Tax Services office.

For a payoff figure and payment options on any county account in that position, call 716-858-8333. Settling the balance before a sale closes keeps a lien from blocking the deed transfer.

City tax, sewer rent, the county bill and any local charges are paid from your sale proceeds at closing. Order payoff figures from both the city and Erie County, since they keep separate books.

  • Ask the city for tax, sewer rent and user fee balances, plus any sidewalk or demolition charge
  • Ask Erie County for the county balance, especially after January when the new county bill posts
  • If a parcel was combined or divided, the city accepts that application only after a full year of city tax, sewer rent and user fee is paid

A cash buyer can close quickly, and the payoffs are deducted the same way as in any other sale. Collect both figures in writing and hand them to the closing attorney so nothing is missed.

Sewer rent arrives with the city's tax billing, and it is easy to overlook because it is not property tax. The department also bills local charges such as sidewalk or demolition costs, and these can stay on a parcel until they are paid. Treat them as part of the payoff. If you are unsure whether anything is attached to your address, ask the city for a full list of balances rather than a tax-only figure.

One more rule affects owners who plan to combine or split a lot before selling. The city takes that application only after a full year of city tax, sewer rent and user fee has been paid, so a parcel with arrears cannot be reconfigured until it is current.

sections.h2: What changes between the city bill and the county bill
sections.html:
It helps to think of two separate ledgers. The city keeps one for tax, sewer rent and user fees, and Erie County keeps another for the county bill. A balance on one does not show up on the other, which is why a seller who clears the city account can still be surprised by a county figure that posts later. After January, when the new county bill posts, ask the county for an updated number.

Each ledger has its own phone line, hours and payment options. Keep the two numbers, 716-851-5733 for the city and 716-858-8333 for the county, together in one place and note the date of every call. A buyer's title company will want the same information, and having it ready lets escrow open without delay.

Fewer than half of Buffalo households own their home, with an owner-occupied rate of 43.0 percent. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $164,200 and median gross rent is $1,046. Neighborhoods such as Elmwood, Allentown, Larkinville and the First Ward each price differently. A lower assessment in the December window feeds into both the city and county bills, so it is worth checking before you list.

sections.h2: Preparing for a quick Buffalo sale
sections.html:
Buffalo sellers often have more than one bill to clear, so start with a short list:

  1. Collect your last city tax and sewer rent bills and the county bill.
  2. Call the city for any sidewalk, demolition or other local charge on the parcel.
  3. Check whether an exemption or STAR registration is active and plan to close it.
  4. Ask both offices for written payoff amounts that are good through your expected closing date.

Doing this before you accept an offer means the figure you negotiate matches what escrow actually pays.

faqs.q: When is the Buffalo grievance period?
faqs.a: Ask the Department of Assessment and Taxation for this year's dates. You file form RP-524 with the department in City Hall Room 101, and a board of city residents reviews it.

faqs.q: When are Buffalo city property taxes due?
faqs.a: Ask the Department of Assessment and Taxation for the current due dates. Erie County bills its part separately and sets its own dates.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Buffalo assessment?
faqs.a: The Department of Assessment and Taxation at 716-851-5733, option 1 for the Assessor. The office is open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. in City Hall at 65 Niagara Square.

faqs.q: Where do I pay the Erie County part of a Buffalo tax bill?
faqs.a: Through Erie County Real Property Tax Services, online or at 95 Franklin Street, Room 100. The tax line is 716-858-8333, and the office can give payoff amounts and payment options.

faqs.q: Can I get a payment plan in Buffalo if I am behind?
faqs.a: The Tax Office helps owners obtain court-ordered payment plans, and it notifies owners facing foreclosure for non-payment. Call 716-851-5733 as soon as you know you cannot pay.
